Do not invent edits or infer an expected overall answer. Return JSON status, concise image-grounded evidence, and confidence (a number from 0 to 1, or null if unavailable). A support check uses pass/fail/unknown. A known negative supporting observation can inform a requested check; it is not automatically uncertainty. Use unknown when the evidence cannot establish the requested fact. Do not count supporting facts as completed edits. Assess only the supplied check, not the overall instruction label.

n1: The binding is underspecified: it contains “(...)” and does not encode the node’s explicit partial-progress criterion. The edited image shows multiple mug-like objects and a blurred blue mug-shaped remnant on the left, while the headphones are also altered; the traces’ confident claim that the mug is clearly right of the headphones does not establish whether the original mug was moved, duplicated, or partly erased. Refine the node’s typed criteria to track the mug from source to edit and distinguish complete relocation from movement toward the right that falls short, while treating duplication/erasure or uncertain object identity as unresolved unless supported by visible evidence. Preserve the requested rightward relation and unrelated-edit exclusion; do not infer partial merely from the reference label. No transport, schema, or dependency failure is reported, so investigate the visual binding/evidence and criterion ambiguity rather than execution.
